evidence:
Most plural and whole-collection asks are graded over the whole collection. Instances checked: (a) hro_bulk 'If any one of them can't go, none of them moves'. The skipping card is first in board order in step 4 and last in board order and selected first in step 8, and there is a 3-into-2 capacity set, each 'with none of the set moved'. This rules out first-only, last-only and partial implementations. (b) hro_undo_activity 'Undo puts every card of that move back'. Step 3 reads all of Y, W and X at their places. The 'any of those cards changed' blockers in steps 4 and 6 change the second card of the set. (c) Activity has 'a readable line ... for every successful action of this session on the job', 'the filter shows all of this job's lines and only this job's' and 'the refused attempts in steps 3 to 9 added no line'. These are whole-collection checks. (d) hro_readonly_roles: 'Every one of those replays is refused', with an explicit carve-out for kinds whose staff control failed. (e) hro_candidate: 'Capture every request ... inspect every response', including SSE and WebSocket frames. (f) hro_long_thread: 'until none remain, with none missing or repeated'. (g) hro_intake_restart: 'everything recorded is unchanged (nothing lost, reordered or duplicated)', re-reading several records after a real restart_app (lesson 15). (h) The constraints gate checks 'exactly one card'. Unchanged guards that are already careful about legitimate side effects: hro_moves says 'never from Activity, whose old rejection line keeps it by design'. hro_pol_live_board moves a card outside the filled stage 'so the board's height does not change'. hro_long_thread and hro_unread_seen read counts 'relative to their values before you act'. The functional prompt's Shared state section grades legs against the state the app actually produced. hro_undo_activity step 5 states that a note and a different card's re-order do not block undo, which matches hireops_rules.md lines 101-102.

DEFECT (P2). hro_unread_seen asserts an exact seeded count: 'the starting read markers give her 1. No other session opens Lena's conversation ... Bar. Lena's count is 1.' Only the polish prompt protects this precondition ('Never use Lena Fischer's conversation', polish/prompt.md line 24). The functional prompt has no such rule. hro_readonly_roles, which runs earlier in the same sequential functional suite (test.sh run_suite uses --max-concurrent-agent 1; criteria are listed in this order), tells the judge as Rafael to do 'one conversation read (open any conversation) and one message send (a suffixed message in that conversation)'. That is a permitted, legitimate send. If the judge picks Lena's Product Designer conversation (APP-301, one of only four seeded conversations with messages, and unread 3 for Rafael), Lena's count becomes 2. hro_unread_seen then fails a correct app, which would be an unchanged-since-seed guard punishing a legitimate side effect of another criterion. app_context.md line 30 itself says 'Other reviews may have added jobs, cards and messages; never rely on a starting count.' The golden sorts conversations by latest message (threads.js line 38), so Lena's is around third after hro_intake_restart's send in Noor's Platform Engineer conversation, and the risk is lower there. A conforming app may list conversations alphabetically by candidate, though. Among threads with messages, 'Lena Fischer' then sorts first, and the judge most plausibly picks the first one. This loses hro_unread_seen's 3.5 of 61 functional weight. No configured judge run has measured it.

NOTES (P3, other instances found). (1) hro_readonly_roles requires that every Observer, candidate and anonymous replay 'returns no workspace data'. The brief says 'gets nothing back' only for the 401 case (hireops_rules.md line 22). Candidate bodies are covered by section 7. For the Observer, a 403 body that repeats the card's current stage and position is not forbidden by the brief and could even be a sensible design for 'put the card back'. Read literally, it would fail. The golden 403 for the Observer is {error} only (index.js line 239), so the golden is not affected. (2) 'Observers and candidates don't move anything' is sampled over seven request kinds: move, multi-card move, reject, undo, add-candidate, open-job and note. Re-order and reopen are not replayed for the Observer or the candidate. An app with a separate, unguarded re-order or reopen endpoint would pass. The golden routes re-ordering through the move endpoint (index.js lines 267 and 334). (3) The undo blockers in steps 4 and 6 always change the last card of the set (X of V,X; W of Y,W). An implementation that checks only the last card is implausible and was not tested. (4) Lesson 1, about hidden requirements in plural bars: apart from note 1, no whole-collection criterion asks for anything absent from the brief.

The raw evidence (scripted golden workspace.cjs) runs each scenario in isolation. It does not model cross-criterion state in a single judge sequence, so the Lena interaction is unmeasured. No configured judge run, Oracle score or model score exists for this candidate.
counterexample: A correct app lists staff conversations alphabetically by candidate name, showing only conversations that have messages, so Lena Fischer's Product Designer conversation is first. In hro_readonly_roles the judge follows 'open any conversation' and sends a suffixed message there as Rafael. Later, in hro_unread_seen, Lena's correct unread count is 2, the criterion's bar 'Lena's count is 1' fails, and the correct app loses 3.5 of 61 functional weight.
suggested_fix: In hro_readonly_roles, make the conversation read and send use a conversation on Rafael's own new job (add a card and open its conversation), and add 'Never open or write in Lena Fischer's conversation except where hro_unread_seen reads her count' to the functional prompt's Shared state section. Optionally, limit 'returns no workspace data' to the candidate and anonymous replays, and add Observer re-order and reopen replays.
